pinnedPlanRegion.definition: From heading RM-301–307/108 through immediately before heading RM-207/401/402. Earlier plan checkpoints are context, not separately approved implementation.

acceptedOwnerInputs.authority: Dedicated revocable reminder-service role; currently eligible Todos, active-owner recipient details, ReminderMail dispatch, and matching-revision sent-field completion only. No general patch/delete, owner impersonation or maintenance authority.
acceptedOwnerInputs.unknownOutcome: No automatic resend, including a new identity or later scheduled scan bypassing the same Todo's unresolved earlier effect.
acceptedOwnerInputs.assessment: Settled product inputs, not implementation proof. No new owner decision is needed merely to reuse the accepted authority direction. Generic retry implementation remains main-owned and is not reviewed here.

existingBuildingBlocks.assessment: Existing api_bearer service_key, service_signed and exchange retain service identity, independent credential revocation and live/fresh authority checks. Service.id is not User.id and owning operator is not an impersonated principal. Direct key authentication or exchanged credential with fresh=true is the minimal worker entry mechanism; cached bounded signed identity alone is insufficient for fresh admission.

Service-member application membership and operation exceptions already have checked models. Exceptions are selected by exact checked entity-owned operation and replace that operation's default subject matrix; they need not grant entity-wide CRUD. Runtime predicates resolve stored membership, not credential role claims.

Read role scope enters SQL before ordering/limit; mutation field policies compose conjunctively for supplied/fixed target fields. Static projection proofs retain stable output shapes and can prohibit recipient-field leakage. Existing examples demonstrate these pieces separately, not the combined reminder worker.

minimalRecommendedPattern.status: Implementation recipe using existing semantic concepts; not claimed compile-pass source on current compiler
minimalRecommendedPattern.membership: One provisioned ReminderRole.worker enum plus protected application-scoped ServiceReminderMembership(service_id: Service.id, role: ReminderRole). No public self-enrollment. Deleting the membership is an implementable immediate role-revocation mechanism; a status/expiry lifecycle may be used only after its predicates are demonstrably enforced in membership SQL.
minimalRecommendedPattern.authentication: Compiler worker obtains a provisioned secret credential through the existing approved secret handoff and authenticates via existing api_bearer. It does not construct PolicyPrincipal from job name, Service ID, owner ID or a trusted-looking host value. Reauthenticate fresh at each admission, including retries; retain policy principal context through nested operations.

operationMatrix.grant: ReminderRole.worker read in named exception only
operationMatrix.guard: Authoritative open, visible, unsent Todo with non-null due_at strictly earlier than the operation instant; required active owner and permitted current recipient before order/limit; deterministic due_at,id selection bounded at 500.

operationMatrix.grant: ReminderRole.worker read in named exception only, with email-readable field narrowing
operationMatrix.guard: Resolve recipient through the same eligible Todo and expected revision, never arbitrary caller-supplied User.id. Separate closed private reminder projection; no authentication_subject, credentials, unrelated owners or general user projection.

operationMatrix.grant: ReminderRole.worker invoke plus the checked ReminderMail effect
operationMatrix.guard: Recheck fresh service credential/authority, membership, Todo revision/eligibility, active owner/current recipient, immutable payload identity and claim/fence/budget inside the admission transaction. Commit possible-dispatch before HTTP and release DB locks before external I/O.

operationMatrix.grant: ReminderRole.worker update in named exception only; return Unit to avoid incidental broad read grant
operationMatrix.guard: Compiler-owned valid outcome for exact intent/key/current fence. Atomically record receipt against its intent and set only reminder_sent_at when Todo still has that schedule revision and remains unsent. Use compiler observation time, not provider accepted_at, as sent mark. Late old receipt cannot mark newer revision.

minimalRecommendedPattern.fieldBoundary: Preserve owner-only ordinary Todo CRUD and user privacy. Restrict service writes on every non-sent semantic field, not just the patch input; a named update exception otherwise inherits unannotated fields. Completion has a fixed one-field set, no PatchTodo, no caller-supplied field list or arbitrary timestamp/receipt authority. Keep derived owner due_at-supplied clear distinct from service completion and client sent-state writes.
minimalRecommendedPattern.noPrivilegeLaundering: A wrapper, alternate entity action, route, nested call, projection or operation-key spelling cannot lend completion authority to general update/delete. Exact job/effect reachability and protected private outcome provenance are required, not a function name or ordinary service credential by itself.
minimalRecommendedPattern.timeAndConcurrency: Candidate selection is not dispatch authority. Coordinate authoritative row/membership/credential checks and possible-dispatch commit so revocation or due-date change before admission prevents dispatch. A change after committed admission may race the already admitted HTTP request as the frozen service contract states; do not claim retroactive external rollback. No DB transaction spans mail.

implementationBlockers.kind: source-derived implementation prerequisite, not a reproduced exploit
implementationBlockers.blocker: EntityPolicyContract holds one scope. Current Todo owner binding resolves Todo scope; User self resolves User scope. Exception-only application ReminderRole does not add a separate operation scope, and both SQL/row runtime helpers require membership.scope == entity scope. Thus copying the existing application service membership into a Todo/User named exception does not establish its role on these entities. Adding a broad base rule is not a safe fix and does not resolve mixed scope cleanly.
implementationBlockers.requiredImplementation: Resolve qualified role scope per subject/operation, preserving resource owner scopes while resolving application memberships independently, and validate exception-only role bindings. Keep SQL and row checks aligned. A per-resource Todo/User membership scheme could avoid the single-scope mismatch but adds provisioning/authority relationships and still cannot prove recipient eligibility or solve field narrowing; do not silently substitute it for the accepted dedicated role.

implementationBlockers.blocker: Field validation checks only base entity grants, so service-only named email-read or sent-update whitelists are rejected as POLICY_FIELD_WIDENS_ENTITY without a broad base grant. Unannotated fields inherit the named operation's update grant; annotating only reminder_sent_at does not deny other fields. Runtime policyFieldEffects is built from listed effects, so an empty policy or read-only policy does not automatically generate an update-denial key. A service-only sent-field policy would also block the existing owner's due_at-supplied derived clear, because derived changed fields participate in write policy checks.
implementationBlockers.requiredImplementation: Make field validation aware of effective named-operation grants without granting ordinary entity effects; generate explicit denial for restricted-but-ungranted effects. Prove exact semantic target-field set and write provenance per checked operation. Preserve the owner's fixed due_at-triggered clear/init path while rejecting arbitrary owner/client sent timestamps; do not solve this by granting service general update or owner arbitrary completion.

implementationBlockers.blocker: Role/field matrices do not themselves encode overdue, active-owner or revision predicates. Current ordinary update representation has one equality selector; generated multi-field update SQL adds lifecycle/policy scope, not a schedule-revision compare-and-set. Page predicates offer equality and optional <=, not the frozen strict due_at < at boundary or an arbitrary active-owner relation. Existing guard:revision syntax and change-log revisions are not proof of an implemented schedule-revision CAS or the required ABA semantics.
implementationBlockers.requiredImplementation: Add the bounded checked query/admission/completion lowering needed for strict live eligibility, correlated active-owner recipient scope and exact private schedule revision. Keep current-row guards in atomic admission/completion SQL or equivalently locked authoritative transactions; never select then perform an unconditional later update. Advance schedule revision for every successful supplied due_at, including equal value, but not omission/failed patch. Integrate the worker with current private state primitives rather than treating host claim/receipt APIs as public policy proof.

membershipRevocationLimit.assessment: Existing emitted membership predicates check member, role and optional scope, not membership lifecycle visibility/status/expiry. DELETE-based revocation is usable; simply declaring a soft-delete/status lifecycle is not proof of revocation enforcement. Concurrent admission requires a defined lock/snapshot cut rather than assuming a previous membership lookup remains current through dispatch commit.

requiredImplementationTests.requirements: Canonical compile-pass worker/service-membership plus Todo/User named exceptions and field whitelists, without service base CRUD; audit shows exact service authentication, role sources, operation keys, reachable effects and sent-only semantic write. Negative unbound/mismatched scope and same UUID in user/service namespaces.

Real authenticated reminder service cannot invoke Todo create/get/list/patch/delete, User disable, arbitrary-recipient reads, owner impersonation, maintenance purge, broad projections or membership self-grant. Wrapper/nested/alternate-route and additional fixed-write mutations cannot bypass operation/field checks; denied mixed patches commit nothing.

Exclude due_at none/equal/future, closed/deleted/sent Todos and inactive owners; deterministic clock tests strictly overdue boundary. Correlate User.email to the eligible Todo/owner/revision and exclude unrelated active users. Owner filtering happens before ordering and 500 limit; no starvation by ineligible owners and no wider recipient result.

Delete membership, revoke credential, disable service or responsible authority, expire/exchange/tamper key, and disable owner between candidate scan and admission: no dispatch. Test bounded exchanged credential with fresh=false versus admission's required fresh=true. Define both sides of concurrent revoke/admission cut with real separate connections.

Exact current receipt marks matching revision once with compiler observation time, never provider clock. Forged caller receipt/time, unrelated intent/key, wrong/stale/expired fence, title/status/due/owner/deleted fields, late A receipt after B, and ABA A-to-B-to-A cannot mark a newer schedule. Valid receipt retained for old intent without updating B.

Ordinary owner CRUD/privacy unchanged; client sent-field input still rejected; due_at supplied equal or changed clears sent and increments schedule revision, omitted due_at does neither, failed patch changes neither. Generated updated_at/change-log effects are separately compiler-owned and audited, not service-authorized patch targets.

Real worker credential/policy admission, possible-dispatch commit then HTTP, crash after acceptance before completion, retry with same ID/fixed payload, unknown FIFO blocking and no resend/new-key bypass. No DB transaction held across provider. These must be worker/golden cases, not merely private host storage tests.

Main-owned integration proves at most 3 total invocations within 1h first valid claim and at most 3 provider attempts/30s per invocation; no reset on restart/new schedule while old delivery unresolved. No credentials, membership internals, recipient email, raw SQL/native errors or provider objects in output/audit/logs. Run equivalent policy and race cases on actual generated SQLite/PostgreSQL adapters.
